Spotify Technology SPOT shares climbed 11% on Thursday after the music-streaming giant reported third-quarter results, highlighted by steady subscriber growth, record gross margins and an increasing focus on artificial intelligence (AI).

Revenue Growth and Record Gross Margin

Spotify reported revenue of nearly €5 billion (about $5.6 billion), broadly in line with market expectations. Premium subscription revenue grew 17% year over year, while ad-supported revenue increased 10%.

Spotify came out with quarterly earnings of $2.85 per share, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.1 per share while it fell from the year-ago level of $3.83 per share. Spotify posted revenues of $5.72 billion in September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $5.70 billion.

However, gross margin reached a record 33%, slightly exceeding Wall Street's estimate of 32.9%. The stock surged 11% during Thursday's trading session. SPOT is now up by only 1.5% for the year 2026.

Subscriber Growth Remains Strong

Spotify continued to expand its user base, with monthly active users rising 11% year over year to 788 million. The company expects monthly active users to reach 818 million in the fourth quarter, while revenue is projected to grow about 15%.

AI Becomes a Bigger Part of Spotify's Strategy

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly shaping Spotify's efforts to improve user engagement and personalization. During the quarter, the company introduced a taste profile feature for U.S. premium subscribers, offering insights into their musical preferences. It also integrated its service with Meta's Muse (read: Should You Tap Meta ETFs on Muse's Success or Wait on the Sidelines?).

However, investors questioned whether AI assistants could weaken Spotify's direct relationship with customers by comparing prices, services and usage across platforms.

Spotify co-CEO Gustav Söderström dismissed these concerns, drawing a parallel with Spotify's existing integrations with Google Maps and Waze. He noted that users have accessed Spotify through these services during their commutes for years without undermining its business model, as mentioned on Yahoo Finance.

Upbeat Outlook

Spotify guided for €820 million of fourth-quarter operating income. The company's fourth-quarter guidance is expected to be 33.8%, up from 33.1% a year earlier.

For the fourth quarter, Spotify expects 316 million subscribers and €5.2 billion of revenue. The revenue figure is a bit below the €5.24 billion analysts expected, according to Bloomberg's consensus, but the subscriber target is above it, per Tikr, as reported by Yahoo Finance.

Spotify Technology S.A. SPOT used its third-quarter 2026 earnings call to emphasize improving advertising trends, subscriber resilience and a slower pace of expense growth.

Reported earnings of $2.85 per share missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.1, while revenues of $5.72 billion exceeded the $5.7 billion estimate. Management emphasized future engagement and profitability.

Spotify Technology Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise
Spotify Technology Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Spotify Technology price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Spotify Technology Quote

SPOT Projects More Growth and Higher Margins in Q4

Chief financial officer Christian Luiga forecast 818 million monthly active users for the fourth quarter, an increase of 30 million, alongside 316 million Premium subscribers, reflecting 10 million net additions.

Luiga guided to €5.2 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, a 33.8% gross margin and €820 million in operating income. Pricing actions and Audiobooks+ add-ons support the revenue outlook.

He said that operating expense growth peaked in the third quarter and should moderate from the fourth quarter into 2027. He cautioned that seasonality and investment timing affect quarterly margins.

Spotify's Advertising Rebuild Gains Traction

Co-CEO Alex Norström said that constant-currency advertising revenue growth accelerated to 9% in the third quarter from 3% in each of the preceding two quarters.

During questions about the advertising recovery, Norström pointed to easier automated buying, improved measurement and greater demand for audio advertisements. Podcast sponsorships contributed.

Luiga said that the company expects to move closer to double-digit advertising growth in the fourth quarter. He noted that advertising represents 10% of revenue, limiting its immediate companywide impact.

SPOT Positions AI Agents as a Distribution Channel

Co-CEO Gustav Söderström argued that integrations with third-party AI agents can broaden access without transferring Spotify's customer listening activity or proprietary taste data to those services.

Addressing concerns about becoming a replaceable back-end provider, Söderström explained that playback remains within Spotify and its recommendation systems continue to interpret user preferences.

He highlighted double-digit gains in content discovery from Spotify's large taste model. Almost 40 million Premium users listen to mixed playlists, with consumption up 90% quarter over quarter.

Spotify Takes Audiobooks Into New Markets

Norström described the expansion of audiobooks from 22 markets to more than 180 by year-end as an opportunity to increase listening days, retention and subscriber lifetime value.

The Morning Bull - US Market Morning Update Friday, Oct, 23 2026

US stocks look set for a cautiously positive open, with S&P 500 futures hovering slightly higher. The single driver this morning is labor strength, as fresh jobless claims signal a still resilient employment backdrop.

Initial unemployment claims came in at 194,000 for the week ended October 17, the lowest level since July. Continuing claims held at 1.728 million. Together, those figures point to limited layoffs and ongoing income support for households.

A labor market that tight keeps wage pressures in focus and can keep borrowing costs sensitive to any upside inflation surprises. At the same time, steady paychecks support revenue expectations in consumer facing businesses and help justify risk exposure in economically sensitive areas.

The unresolved question is how long the Federal Reserve can tolerate this level of labor resilience without shifting its rate stance. This afternoon's US manufacturing and services PMI readings could quickly reset that debate if activity diverges from expectations.

Stocks to Watch Before the Opening Bell

PG&E (PCG)

PG&E reaffirmed its 2026 and 2027 non GAAP core earnings guidance and flagged a US$2b cut to its 2027 capital plan, along with a 2% to 4% target reduction in non fuel operating and maintenance expenses. Management is also weighing a possible separation of the gas unit if wildfire policy does not change, while lobbying for legislative relief.

Alnylam Pharmaceuticals (ALNY)

Alnylam reported early Phase 1b data for brezosiran in Huntington's disease, showing robust, dose dependent lowering of mutant huntingtin protein in cerebrospinal fluid with encouraging safety. The drug could be dosed twice yearly based on the durability seen so far. Management plans a placebo controlled pivotal study in 2027, subject to regulatory alignment.

United Therapeutics (UTHR)

United Therapeutics authorized an additional US$2b share repurchase program that runs through October 21, 2027. The board pointed to a strong balance sheet and free cash flow as support for this capital plan. Investors will likely focus on how aggressively the buyback is used and how it fits alongside spending on pipeline and other long term goals.

Top Movers

Waste Connections (WCN) surged 9.86% after a Q3 beat, a raised 2026 outlook, a higher dividend and heavy buybacks reinforced confidence.

On its third quarter of 2026 earnings call, held on Oct. 22, 2026, Spotify (NYSE:SPOT) announced total revenue reached 5 billion euros, up 14% at constant currency. Free cash flow reached 3.2 billion euros over the past 12 months. Three takeaways from management stand out for long-term investors.

1. Proprietary Taste Models Drive Content Discovery and User Engagement

Investments in artificial intelligence are improving recommendation quality across the platform. Better recommendations keep subscribers engaged longer and strengthen long-term user retention.

Our taste model investments are already paying off. Early deployments show double-digit gains in content discovery, and our users are spending more time in select algorithmic sets.
-- Christian Luiga, Chief Financial Officer

2. Global Audiobook Rollout Expands Subscriber Value and Platform Engagement

Catalog expansion beyond music increases daily platform usage among subscribers. Higher active days improve retention while creating new add-on revenue opportunities.

We have increased our audiobooks listenership by 40%. This is even before launching to the rest of the world. We have seen listening hours grow as well.
-- Alex Norström, Co-Chief Executive Officer

3. Subscriber Base Scaling Shows Multiyear Growth Durability

Consistent annual additions demonstrate broad appeal across developed and emerging markets. A growing base creates a compounding foundation for recurring subscription revenue.

When we went public in 2018, we had 71 million subscribers. Since then, every single year, we've been adding 25 million subs or more. This year, we expect to reach 316 million subscribers.
-- Alex Norström, Co-Chief Executive Officer

Looking Ahead

Revenue momentum accelerates across subscription and advertising channels, supported by lower operating expenses, or OpEx. The platform holds structural advantages in global distribution, proprietary listener taste data, and multi-format audio content, while focusing on margin expansion and capital return.

OpEx growth is now coming down meaningfully, and we expect that moderation to continue into 2027. We see that this year's incremental OpEx is driving multiple benefits to our business.
-- Christian Luiga, Chief Financial Officer

As monetization deepens through add-on features and pricing power, compounding cash flow supports organic investments and share buybacks.

We remain confident in our path and expect another year of progress toward delivering on our 2030 goals. We are well-positioned to continue compounding growth, profitability, and free cash flow.
-- Christian Luiga, Chief Financial Officer

Strategic Performance and Operational Context

Management attributes the quarter's success to 'durability at scale,' noting that the company has consistently added 25 million or more subscribers annually since 2018 despite macro headwinds and price increases.

The 140 basis point year-over-year gross margin expansion was driven by a deliberate balance between high-engagement content acquisition and operational efficiencies.

Advertising revenue growth accelerated to 9% as the company began to realize the benefits of a multi-quarter rebuild of its automated biddable sales channels and podcast sponsorship products.

Strategic positioning is focused on 'anticipation' rather than just extrapolation, specifically regarding the shift toward an agentic media platform where Spotify acts as an intelligent assistant.

The company is optimizing its MAU funnel in emerging markets like India and Indonesia by introducing 'business positive' friction, such as better data hygiene and migrating users to higher-retention device clients.

Management views the Swedish market—where nearly 50% of the population pays for Spotify—as a blueprint for global potential, contrasting it with the current sub-4% global penetration.

Outlook and Strategic Initiatives

Q4 guidance assumes a moderation in operating expense growth, following a peak in Q3, as the company shifts from a heavy investment phase toward sustainable margin expansion.

The expansion of audiobooks to over 180 markets by year-end is expected to enhance subscriber lifetime value and active listening days, serving as a global growth engine.

Management expects advertising to continue its progress toward double-digit growth in Q4, supported by the scaling of automated channels and the Spotify Partner Program.

Future monetization strategy relies on a 'value to price ratio' framework, where continuous product enrichment (like AI features and remixes) justifies future pricing actions and add-on tiers.

The company anticipates that its 'Large Taste Model' will drive billions of incremental listening hours by improving content discovery and user retention through personalized algorithmic sets.

Capital Allocation and Structural Changes

Spotify has neutralized 2026 employee equity dilution by repurchasing 2.2 million shares for $1.1 billion, signaling a shift toward returning excess cash to shareholders.

The company maintains a strong cash position of $9.9 billion to preserve 'strategic flexibility' for potential inorganic growth opportunities or opportunistic buybacks.

Social charges of EUR 22 million were EUR 13 million higher than forecasted due to share price volatility, though this was offset by favorability in marketing and personnel costs.

The launch of Creator Memberships and the expansion of the Spotify Partner Program represent a strategic move to capture the 'power law' of superfan monetization.
